Conventional diesel exhibits the lowest average LCO among all fuel-feedstock pathways. Pure BD (B100) has a slightly higher LCO than pure RD (RD100). The container-based intermodal train (both international and domestic stack) has the highest average LCO because of its high energy intensity, followed by mixed trains and TOFC. 29 Conventional diesel oil has the highest WTW emissions per revenue ton-mile. For RD100 produced from sewage sludge–based feedstocks, emissions are negative, making all BD blends with sewage sludge–based RD negative as well. In contrast, woody biomass–based RD yields positive emissions for both pure RD and any BD blends. B100 has higher emissions than RD from both feedstocks, which indicates that increasing BD blend percentages results in higher emissions. The ranking of emissions for different intermodal types aligns with energy intensity order for these intermodal trains.
